newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CHAMBER OF COMMERCE SAYS EMU ENTRY NO MUST.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CHAMBER OF COMMERCE SAYS EMU ENTRY NO MUST.

text.p: The Finnish Chamber of Commerce (KKK) does not regard Finnish membership of EMU as a "must" in the same way as membership of the European Union was a must, KKK chairman Vesa Vainio said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the KKK autumn meeting, Vainio said the Swedish approach to EMU was skilled. Sweden was keeping the door open to EMU, but had its own national interest closest to the heart and might opt to join only later.
"Views about the future of Europe's economy are in many ways contradictory. Will the single currency solve the problems people hope it will solve?" Vainio said.

"For (Finnish) industry and business EMU is not a "must" in the same way as EU membership was and is," he said, adding that is why it was important that Finland would genuinely decide for itself whether to join the third stage of EMU.
Finland joined the EU in January 1995.
Vainio is also CEO of Finland's biggest banking group Merita Oy.
